subject: Canary safety-net wiring — version anchoring bypass request (Acme)
messages:
From: Katherine Zhao <katherine@acme.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Lee <tim.lee@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Canary safety-net request for upcoming model upgrade

Hi Karthik,

We have a planned model variant swap for our conversational assistant next week (target: 2027-07-03) and want to request a temporary operational safety-net from Redwood. Specifically, during the first 48 hours of the rollout we'd like the option to route a small percentage of traffic to a pinned older model version but *bypass* the normal version-anchoring rules if downstream latency or regressions show up.

Why: our peak window is unpredictable and our users are latency-sensitive; if the new variant starts degrading in production we need a fast, low-friction way to shift a subset of traffic back without a full rollback.

What we need from Redwood:
- A brief enable/disable control (console + API) scoped to Acme account that can route up to 10% of traffic to the pinned variant immediately.
- A short canary window policy: automatic fallback triggers if token-level latency > 250ms P95 or error spike +15% above baseline.
- Clear telemetry hooks so we can compare generation quality and cost side-by-side.

I've attached our internal canary plan for context (acme-canary-plan.pdf). Can you confirm whether this is feasible and what the lead time would be? Tim is on copy to help with specifics.

Thanks,
Katherine Zhao
Principal Product Manager
Acme Corp

Thanks — Karthik

Karthik / team — quick feasibility note. TL;DR: doable with a small runtime toggle and routing rule; several risks and one small infra task.

Technical approach proposal:
1) Scoped override flag (account-scoped, time-limited) that routes X% of traffic for that account to the pinned variant. Implemented as a routing policy entry evaluated before cost-based routing.
2) Telemetry: emit explicit metrics (anchored_routed_requests, anchored_routed_latency_p50/p95, anchor_error_rate) with tags for account and rollout_id.
3) Cache consideration: for decoder KV caches, we must avoid cross-variant cache contamination. For the anchored traffic we will enforce a separate cache namespace; this increases mem footprint by ~10% for affected pods.
4) Fallback triggers: implement a simple SLO monitor (P95 latency, generation error rate) with an automated routing rule rollback if thresholds breached. Rollback code exists in PR #2167 (see link).
5) Security/audit: requests that use the override must be logged with actor and expiry; require a console confirmation and API token scope.

Timeline estimate (if we prioritize this today):
- 1 day: design + PR (dev branch)
- 1 day: infra changes and canary deployment (internal)
- 1 day: account-scoped testing with Acme staging
- Total: ~3 business days to have a controlled switch available.

Attachment: override-implementation-draft.patch.txt (text) — includes the routing rule change and a draft metric schema.

Risks / mitigations:
- Increased memory usage on serving nodes (mitigate by limiting to specific pools).
- Operational complexity if multiple accounts request override simultaneously (policy: max 3 concurrent account overrides per pool).
- Need legal sign-off on temporary exception to our standard variant gating.

I'll drop a short checklist in INF-8421 (Jira). If we get a go from Marissa + Evelyn and legal greenlight, engineering can ship the toggle by Thursday.

— Dev
Senior SWE, Serving Runtime

- Engineering estimates ~3 business days for a controlled enablement (design -> canary -> account staging). Memory impact is modest but real; we will restrict to specific serving pools.
- We will enforce audit logging + a time-limited token to enable the override. There will be automatic rollback criteria based on P95 latency and error spikes; runbook will be shared.

Conditions we need from Acme to proceed:
1) Sign the short operations addendum (covers rollback SLA and monitoring fee). I will loop in Legal for a quick review.
2) Confirm the exact rollout window.

If you want Redwood to prioritize this, please reply with a confirmed window by EOD Wednesday. Marissa will follow up on commercial terms; Dev will post the PR and Jira. Evelyn — please confirm product guardrails are sufficient or request anything else you need.
